nodes.name: Ceva's Theorem (classical)
nodes.statement: Let $\Delta P_0P_1P_2$ be a triangle, and let points $Q_0,Q_1,Q_2$ lie on the edges opposite to $P_0,P_1,P_2$. Then the cevians $P_iQ_i$ have nonempty intersection iff $\frac{P_0Q_1}{Q_1P_2}\frac{P_2Q_0}{Q_0P_1}\frac{P_1Q_2}{Q_2P_0}=1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Three cevians of a triangle are concurrent iff a certain ratio product equals one.
assumptions: $Q_i$ lies on the edge of $\Delta P_0P_1P_2$ opposite vertex $P_i$ for $i\in\{0,1,2\}$
conclusions: The cevians $P_iQ_i$ ($i\in\{0,1,2\}$) have nonempty intersection iff $\frac{P_0Q_1}{Q_1P_2}\frac{P_2Q_0}{Q_0P_1}\frac{P_1Q_2}{Q_2P_0}=1$
nodes.origin_citation: Yusuf al-Mu'taman ibn Hud (classical Ceva's theorem)

nodes.name: Simplex and its interior
nodes.statement: For points $P_0,\dots,P_n$ in general position in $\mathbb{R}^n$, the $n$-simplex is $\mathbf{S}=\Delta P_0P_1\dots P_n$. Its interior $\interior{\mathbf{S}}$ consists of points $\sum_{k=0}^n\alpha_k P_k$ with $\sum\alpha_k=1$ and all $\alpha_k>0$.

nodes.name: Subsimplicial face, facet, and $\mathbf{S}_i$
nodes.statement: Any $k+1$ vertices from $\{P_0,\dots,P_n\}$ span a $k$-dimensional subsimplicial face (or $k$-face) of $\mathbf{S}$. When $k=n-1$ it is called a facet, and $\mathbf{S}_i$ denotes the facet opposite vertex $P_i$.

nodes.name: $k$-cevian and its foot
nodes.statement: For $U=\{u_1,\dots,u_k\}\subset\{0,\dots,n\}$ and complement $U'=\{v_1,\dots,v_l\}$ with $k+l=n+1$, pick $Q_{U'}\in\interior{\Delta P_{v_1}\dots P_{v_l}}$. The simplex $\Delta Q_{U'}P_{u_1}\dots P_{u_k}$ is a $k$-cevian of $\mathbf{S}$, and $Q_{U'}$ is its foot.

nodes.name: Family $\mathfrak{R}$ of $k$-cevians
nodes.statement: Selecting one foot $Q_{U'}$ for each of the $\binom{n+1}{k}$ choices of $U$ produces a family $\mathfrak{R}$ of $\binom{n+1}{k}$ $k$-cevians of $\mathbf{S}$.

nodes.name: $l$-face $\mathbf{L}$ and subfamily $\mathfrak{R}_{\mathbf{L}}$
nodes.statement: For an $l$-face $\mathbf{L}=\Delta P_{j_0}\dots P_{j_l}$ with $J=\{j_0,\dots,j_l\}$ and complement $J'=\{i_1,\dots,i_{k-1}\}$, each facet $\mathbf{L}_t$ ($t\in J$) contains exactly one foot $Q_{[t]}=Q_{J\setminus\{t\}}$ of a $k$-cevian $C_t=\Delta Q_{[t]}P_tP_{i_1}\dots P_{i_{k-1}}$. The subfamily $\mathfrak{R}_{\mathbf{L}}$ has $l+1$ elements.

nodes.name: Induced cevian $c_t$ in $\mathbf{L}$
nodes.statement: Given $\mathbf{L}$ and $C_t\in\mathfrak{R}_{\mathbf{L}}$ with foot $Q_{[t]}\in\interior{\mathbf{L}}$, the induced cevian in $\mathbf{L}$ is $c_t=C_t\cap\mathbf{L}=\Delta Q_{[t]}P_t$. The collection of induced $1$-cevians in $\mathbf{L}$ is denoted $\mathfrak{r}_{\mathbf{L}}$.

nodes.name: Multipede and induced multipede
nodes.statement: For an $m$-simplex $\mathbf{T}$ with face collection $\mathcal{F}$, a set $\{A_{\mathbf{F}}\}_{\mathbf{F}\in\mathcal{F}}$ with $A_{\mathbf{F}}\in\interior{\mathbf{F}}$ is a multipede. A point $A_{\mathbf{T}}$ induces such a multipede when $A_{\mathbf{T}}, A_{\mathbf{T}_i}, P_i$ are collinear, and the same collinearity holds recursively on every face.
nodes.origin_citation: Samet 2021, An Extension of Ceva's Theorem to n-Simplices

nodes.name: Partial order $\preceq$ from multipede inclusion
nodes.statement: Define $P\preceq Q$ if $P$ lies in the multipede induced by $Q$ (equivalently, the multipede induced by $P$ is contained in that induced by $Q$). For any vertex $P_i$ and any $Q$ in the interior of a face containing $P_i$, set $P_i\preceq Q$.

nodes.name: Case $n=3$, $k=2$
nodes.statement: In $\mathbf{S}=\Delta P_0P_1P_2P_3$ with $U=\{2,3\}$ and $Q_{U'}\in\interior{\Delta P_0P_1}$, $C=\Delta Q_{U'}P_2P_3$ is a $2$-cevian. With $\mathbf{L}=\Delta P_0P_1P_3$ the induced cevian is $c_3=\Delta Q_{[3]}P_3$, recovering the classical Witczyński/Buba-Brzozowa setting.

nodes.name: Case $n=4$, $k=2$
nodes.statement: In $\mathbf{S}=\Delta P_0P_1P_2P_3P_4$ with $U=\{2,4\}$ and $Q_{U'}\in\interior{\Delta P_0P_1P_3}$, $C=\Delta Q_{U'}P_2P_4$ is a $2$-cevian. Here $\mathbf{L}=\Delta P_0P_1P_2P_3$ and $c_2=\Delta Q_{[2]}P_2$. The cevian $C$ is neither a segment nor of codimension one — a case not previously treated.

nodes.name: Main equivalence (concurrence vs. faces)
nodes.statement: For a family $\mathfrak{R}$ of $k$-cevians in $\mathbf{S}$: (1) $\exists X\in\interior{\mathbf{S}}$ with $X\in\bigcap\mathfrak{R}$; (2) for every $l$-face $\mathbf{L}$, $\bigcap\mathfrak{r}_{\mathbf{L}}\neq\emptyset$. The two conditions are equivalent.
assumptions: $\mathfrak{R}$ is a family of $k$-cevians with $1\leq k<n$ and $k+l=n+1$
conclusions: $\bigcap\mathfrak{R}$ contains a point in $\interior{\mathbf{S}}$ iff $\bigcap\mathfrak{r}_{\mathbf{L}}\neq\emptyset$ for every $l$-face $\mathbf{L}$

nodes.name: Multipede coincidence on a common face
nodes.statement: Fix an $l$-face $\mathbf{L}$, let $Q_{[i]},Q_{[j]}$ be feet of $k$-cevians in the interiors of $\mathbf{L}_i,\mathbf{L}_j$ and let $A,B\in\interior{\mathbf{F}}\subset\mathbf{L}$ satisfy $A\preceq Q_{[i]}$ and $B\preceq Q_{[j]}$. Then condition (2) of Theorem~2.1 implies $A=B$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.2
nodes.statement: Take $X\in\bigcap\mathfrak{r}_{\mathbf{L}}$; then $Q_{[i]}\preceq X$ and $Q_{[j]}\preceq X$, hence $A\preceq X$ and $B\preceq X$. Since $A,B\in\interior{\mathbf{F}}$, [Samet 2021, Proposition 1] gives $A=B$.

nodes.name: Single intersection point per $t$-face
nodes.statement: Let $W$ be the set of points generated by all $k$-cevian feet. If condition (2) holds, then for every $t$-face $\mathbf{T}$ ($1\leq t\leq l-1$), $|W\cap\interior{\mathbf{T}}|=1$.

nodes.name: Reformulation of condition (2) via $\preceq$
nodes.statement: Condition (2) of Theorem~2.1 is equivalent to: for every $l$-face $\mathbf{L}$ there exists $X$ such that $Q_{[t]}\preceq X$ for all feet $Q_{[t]}$ of cevians $C_t\in\mathfrak{R}_{\mathbf{L}}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.1 (main equivalence)
nodes.statement: Forward direction by extracting a point $\hat X$ on each induced cevian via barycentric uniqueness; reverse direction by induction on the cevian dimension $k$, using known $n\in\{2,3\}$ cases as base and Buba-Brzozowa's $k=n-1$ result.

nodes.name: Forward setup: assume (1) and pick $\mathbf{L}$
nodes.statement: WLOG $\mathbf{L}=\Delta P_0\dots P_l$, so each $C_t\in\mathfrak{R}_{\mathbf{L}}$ is $\Delta Q_{[t]}P_tP_{l+1}\dots P_n$ for $t\in\{0,\dots,l\}$. Pick $X\in\bigcap\mathfrak{R}\subset\interior{\mathbf{S}}$.
nodes.statement_latex: Without loss of generality $\mathbf{L}=\Delta P_0\dots P_l$ and $X\in\bigcap\mathfrak{R}$.

nodes.name: Express $X$ in two barycentric forms
nodes.statement: Write $X=\sum_{m=0}^n\alpha_mP_m$ and, since $X\in C_t\cap C_s$, also $X=\beta_1Q_{[t]}+\beta_2P_t+\sum_{m=l+1}^n\alpha_mP_m=\gamma_1Q_{[s]}+\gamma_2P_s+\sum_{m=l+1}^n\alpha_mP_m$ (equation (2.1)).

nodes.name: Construct $\hat X$ on $\Delta Q_{[t]}P_t$
nodes.statement: Set $\hat X:=\frac{\beta_1}{\beta_1+\beta_2}Q_{[t]}+\frac{\beta_2}{\beta_1+\beta_2}P_t\in\Delta Q_{[t]}P_t$, then claim $\hat X\in\Delta Q_{[s]}P_s$.

nodes.name: Cancel the common tail $K$ via barycentric uniqueness
nodes.statement: Let $K=\sum_{m=l+1}^n\alpha_mP_m$. Equation (2.1) gives $(\beta_1+\beta_2)\hat X+K=(\gamma_1+\gamma_2)\bigl(\frac{\gamma_1}{\gamma_1+\gamma_2}Q_{[s]}+\frac{\gamma_2}{\gamma_1+\gamma_2}P_s\bigr)+K$, and $\beta_1+\beta_2=1-\sum_{m=l+1}^n\alpha_m=\gamma_1+\gamma_2$, so $\hat X=\frac{\gamma_1}{\gamma_1+\gamma_2}Q_{[s]}+\frac{\gamma_2}{\gamma_1+\gamma_2}P_s\in\bigcap\mathfrak{r}_{\mathbf{L}}$.

nodes.name: Reverse direction — base cases and induction setup
nodes.statement: Assume (2). For $n\in\{2,3\}$ the implication is classical (Ceva, Witczyński/Buba-Brzozowa, Samet). For $n\geq 4$ induct on $k$, base case $k=n-1$ from [Buba-Brzozowa 2000]. Inductive hypothesis: result holds for $k$; prove it for $k-1$.

nodes.name: Build a $k$-cevian family from $(k-1)$-cevian feet
nodes.statement: By Remark~2.3 each $(l-1)$-face $\mathbf{F}=\Delta P_{v_1}\dots P_{v_l}$ contains exactly one point $Q_{U'}$ generated by feet of $\mathfrak{R}^{k-1}$. Form $C=\Delta Q_{U'}P_{u_1}\dots P_{u_k}$ over the $\binom{n+1}{k}$ choices to obtain a family $\mathfrak{R}$ of $k$-cevians satisfying (2) (Remark~2.4).

nodes.name: Apply the inductive hypothesis to obtain $X$
nodes.statement: By the inductive hypothesis applied to $\mathfrak{R}$, there exists $X\in\bigcap\mathfrak{R}$.

nodes.name: Show $X$ lies in every $(k-1)$-cevian
nodes.statement: Take $\hat C=\Delta\hat QP_{i_1}\dots P_{i_{k-1}}$ in $\mathfrak{R}^{k-1}$ with $\hat Q\in\interior{\mathbf{L}}$. Writing $X\in C_t$ and matching coordinates yields $\hat Q=\frac{\beta_1}{\beta_1+\beta_2}Q_{[t]}+\frac{\beta_2}{\beta_1+\beta_2}P_t$; setting $\hat\omega=\beta_1+\beta_2$ and $\omega_m=\alpha_{i_m}$ shows $X\in\hat C$.

nodes.name: Main result (volumetric form)
nodes.statement: Let $\mathfrak{R}$ be a family of $k$-cevians in $\mathbf{S}$. Then (1') $\bigcap\mathfrak{R}\neq\emptyset$; (2') for every $l$-face $\mathbf{L}$ and every uniform or mixed fan $\{(F_z,L_z,M_z)\mid z\in\mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z}\}$, $\prod_{z\in\mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z}}\frac{\mathrm{Vol}(L_z)}{\mathrm{Vol}(M_z)}=1$. Conditions (1') and (2') are equivalent.
assumptions: $\mathfrak{R}$ is a family of $k$-cevians in $\mathbf{S}$ with $1\leq k<n$
conclusions: $\bigcap\mathfrak{R}\neq\emptyset$ iff for every $l$-face $\mathbf{L}$ and every uniform or mixed fan, $\prod_{z\in\mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z}}\frac{\mathrm{Vol}(L_z)}{\mathrm{Vol}(M_z)}=1$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.5
nodes.statement: Condition (2') of Theorem~2.5 is equivalent to condition (2) of Theorem~2.1, as shown in [Samet 2021]. Combined with Theorem~2.1, this yields the equivalence (1') $\Leftrightarrow$ (2').

nodes.name: Special cases of Theorem 2.5
nodes.statement: Theorem~2.5 specializes to: (i) classical Ceva ($n=2$, $k=1$); (ii) Witczyński's theorem ($n=3$, $k=2$); (iii) Buba-Brzozowa's theorem ($n>2$, $k=n-1$); (iv) Samet's theorem ($n>2$, $k=1$).

nodes.name: Witczyński's theorem (cited)
nodes.statement: Ceva-type concurrence theorem for tetrahedra using $(n-1)$-dimensional cevians, recovered as the $n=3$, $k=2$ case of Theorem~2.5.
conclusions: Concurrence of the family of $(n-1)$-cevians is characterized by a Ceva-type ratio identity

nodes.name: Buba-Brzozowa's theorem (cited)
nodes.statement: Ceva-type concurrence theorem for $n$-dimensional simplices with $(n-1)$-dimensional cevians; serves as the base case $k=n-1$ of the inductive proof of Theorem~2.1.
conclusions: The family of $(n-1)$-cevians has nonempty intersection iff a Ceva-type ratio identity holds

nodes.name: Samet's theorem (cited)
nodes.statement: Extension of Ceva's theorem to $n$-simplices with $1$-dimensional cevians; recovered as the $k=1$ case of Theorem~2.5.
conclusions: The family of $1$-cevians has nonempty intersection iff the multipede / volumetric Ceva-type condition holds
nodes.origin_citation: Samet 2021, An Extension of Ceva's Theorem to n-Simplices

nodes.name: Mixed-dimension Ceva for the tetrahedron
nodes.statement: For $\Delta P_0P_1P_2P_3$ with $\mathfrak{R}=\{\Delta Q_{\{0,1\}}P_2P_3,\Delta Q_{\{0,2\}}P_1P_3,\Delta Q_{\{0,3\}}P_1P_2,\Delta Q_{\{1,2,3\}}P_0\}$ and feet $Q_{\{i,j\}}\preceq Q_{\{1,2,3\}}$, $\bigcap\mathfrak{R}\neq\emptyset$ iff $\frac{P_iQ_{\{i,j\}}}{Q_{\{i,j\}}P_j}\frac{P_jQ_{\{j,k\}}}{Q_{\{j,k\}}P_k}\frac{P_kQ_{\{k,i\}}}{Q_{\{k,i\}}P_i}=1$ for every $0\leq i<j<k\leq 3$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.1
nodes.statement: Construct auxiliary $C_1,C_2,C_3$ and $\mathfrak{R}'=\{C_1,C_2,C_3\}\cup\mathfrak{R}\setminus\{\Delta Q_{\{1,2,3\}}P_0\}$. Apply Buba-Brzozowa's theorem to $\mathfrak{R}'$ in both directions, and use convexity along the line $P_0X$ to identify $Y=Q_{\{1,2,3\}}$.

nodes.name: Set up auxiliary family $\mathfrak{R}'$
nodes.statement: Define $C_1=\Delta Q_{\{2,3\}}P_0P_1$, $C_2=\Delta Q_{\{1,3\}}P_0P_2$, $C_3=\Delta Q_{\{1,2\}}P_0P_3$ and $\mathfrak{R}'=\{C_1,C_2,C_3\}\cup\mathfrak{R}\setminus\{\Delta Q_{\{1,2,3\}}P_0\}$.

nodes.name: (1)$\Rightarrow$(2): apply Buba-Brzozowa to $\mathfrak{R}'$
nodes.statement: Take $X\in\bigcap\mathfrak{R}$; then $X\in\Delta Q_{\{1,2,3\}}P_0\subset C_i$ for $i\in\{1,2,3\}$, so $X\in\bigcap\mathfrak{R}'$. Buba-Brzozowa's theorem applied to $\mathfrak{R}'$ yields the ratio identity (2).

nodes.name: (2)$\Rightarrow$(1): identify $Y=Q_{\{1,2,3\}}$ via convexity
nodes.statement: Buba-Brzozowa gives $X\in\bigcap\mathfrak{R}'$. Consider line $P_0X$ and $Y\in P_0X\cap\Delta P_1P_2P_3$. Each $C_i$ is convex and contains $P_0,Y$, so $\Delta P_0Y\subset C_i$, forcing $Y=Q_{\{1,2,3\}}$ and hence $X\in\Delta Q_{\{1,2,3\}}P_0$.

nodes.name: General mixed-dimension Ceva theorem
nodes.statement: Find conditions for the non-emptiness of a family of cevians of varying dimensions, in which Theorem~2.5 would appear as a special case.
